summary: The positive rescaling preserves balance, strict negativity, exact affine minorants, cap halfspaces, and global support minimality. The predecessor construction applies to each rescaled circuit and yields the stated same-base Minkowski fibers. Support-function convergence gives Hausdorff convergence on every positive-volume lattice fiber, convex-body volume continuity and finite lattice support give convergence of W, and the boundary approach justifies the infimum bound. A vertex optimizer of the finite barycentric LP has affinely independent positive support of size at most rho+1; complementary slackness in the elementary nonnegative-sum form gives contact there. At every contact fiber, the proposed density contradiction correctly proves that the cap above the half-metronoid support level has volume at most a_z/2. The mass-loss inequalities, near-identity implication, quantifier passage over circuits, notation, and uses of the accepted predecessor fact are all consistent, including degenerate affine dimension and boundary cases.
